policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's proper name 'Hamutal' distinguishes the qere חֲמוּטַל from the ketiv spelling חמיטל.
ASV 'put him in prison' does not distinguish qere בֵית from ketiv בבית; the English locative wording permits either reading.
ASV 'the height of the one pillar' expresses the construct relation marked by qere קוֹמַת, distinguishing it from ketiv קומה.
ASV 'out of prison' gives no spelling or wording distinction between qere הַכְּלוּא and ketiv הכליא; both remain compatible.
ASV 'the kings' explicitly represents the definite article in qere הַמְּלָכִים, distinguishing it from ketiv מלכים.
